m1_status.conclusion: All 4 mechanisms necessary. No subtraction possible. DINO-sty changes within noise (±0.002). Path to DINO-sty≥0.50 must come from M2 architectural additions.
m1_status.key_finding: LL FM is most critical (-0.035 DINO-con if removed). Edge/terminal/ep_content all slightly hurt DINO-sty but help content preservation. No clean subtraction for DINO-sty gain.

D1_gram_matrix.conclusion: w=1.0 is optimal: CLIP-S +0.0023, 1-LPIPS +0.0025, DINO-sty +0.0018 (near-lossless micro-gain). w=5.0 over-strengthens: 1-LPIPS +0.019 but CLIP-S -0.0011 and DINO-sty -0.0008. Gram helps style slightly but does not scale.
D1_gram_matrix.key_finding: 2nd-order inter-channel correlations (Gram) give micro-gain at w=1.0 but do not scale. DINO-sty ceiling ~0.478. Need higher-order or different mechanism for meaningful gain.

D2_high_order_moment.conclusion: D2 FAILED: High-order moment matching trades style for content. CLIP-S -0.0084, DINO-sty -0.0030, but 1-LPIPS +0.013 and DINO-con +0.011. Same pattern as D1 w=5.0: stronger distribution constraints push output toward content, away from style. Statistical moment matching is wrong direction for DINO-sty.

D4_film_heads.conclusion: D4 FAILED: FiLM at velocity head disrupts flow matching. 1-LPIPS -0.117 (catastrophic content loss), DINO-sty -0.016, DINO-con -0.077. Direct style injection at velocity prediction point is harmful — velocity head must remain pure function of backbone features. Style must come through backbone cross-attention only.

inference_sweep.conclusion: ALL 4 inference-time parameter overrides FAILED catastrophically. Every metric degraded: CLIP-S -0.012~-0.015, 1-LPIPS -0.215~-0.251 (!), DINO-sty -0.050~-0.055, DINO-con -0.086~-0.124. Baseline checkpoint is already optimally tuned for its trained parameters. DINO-sty ceiling at 0.4762 is TRAINING-LEVEL, not inference-level. Cannot be broken by WCT/extrap adjustment.

D6_intrinsic_style_consistency.conclusion: D6 FAILED: CLIP-S=0.7181(+0.001), 1-LPIPS=0.5931(-0.108!), DINO-sty=0.4623(-0.014), DINO-con=0.7376(-0.068). ROOT CAUSE: intrinsic_style_cnn is trainable and co-optimized with generation path → encoder degeneration. Model minimizes cosine loss by making encoder output similar vectors regardless of input, rather than making generated images more stylistically similar. Same pattern as D4: direct style signal disrupts content-style balance. Self-supervised style loss with trainable encoder is a dead end.

D7_backbone_capacity_expansion.description: D7 (num_res_blocks=6, lr=2e-4) NaN crashed at epoch 1 75%. D7b (lr=5e-5, grad_clip=0.5) trained stably 15 epochs, 1,219,922 params (+15%).
D7_backbone_capacity_expansion.conclusion: D7b FAILED: deeper backbone (6 layers) REDUCED all metrics. CLIP-S=0.7092(-0.008), 1-LPIPS=0.6452(-0.056), DINO-sty=0.4591(-0.017), DINO-con=0.7798(-0.025). ROOT CAUSE: deeper network has more style injection points but also more content abstraction — the additional cross-attention layers over-stylize and destroy content structure. The 4-layer backbone is already at the optimal depth for the style-content tradeoff. Depth scaling is NOT the path to DINO-sty>=0.50.

D8_width_scaling.description: D8 tested 3 width-scaling configs: D8a (heads 4->8), D8b (base_dim 64->96), D8c (heads 8 + gate 0.3->0.5). All trained stably 15 epochs.
D8_width_scaling.conclusion: ALL 3 D8 width-scaling configs FAILED. D8a: CLIP-S=0.7214(+0.005), 1-LPIPS=0.5921(-0.109), DINO-sty=0.4620(-0.014), DINO-con=0.7329(-0.072). D8b: CLIP-S=0.7198(+0.003), 1-LPIPS=0.5566(-0.144), DINO-sty=0.4565(-0.020), DINO-con=0.7046(-0.101). D8c: CLIP-S=0.7181(+0.001), 1-LPIPS=0.5743(-0.127), DINO-sty=0.4526(-0.024), DINO-con=0.7086(-0.097). ROOT CAUSE: width scaling (more heads or wider dim) increases capacity but the extra capacity is used for content reconstruction (1-LPIPS drops) NOT style. More heads/wider dim lets the model memorize content better, reducing reliance on style features. The baseline 4-head/64-dim config is already optimal — it forces the model to rely on style injection for reconstruction. Width scaling is a DEAD END.

D9_loss_reweighting.description: D9 tested 3 loss reweighting configs: D9a (swd 12->16), D9b (swd 12->20 + content 1.0->0.5), D9c (swd 12->24). All trained stably 15 epochs.
D9_loss_reweighting.conclusion: ALL 3 D9 loss reweighting configs FAILED. D9a: CLIP-S=0.7230(+0.006), 1-LPIPS=0.5787(-0.122), DINO-sty=0.4639(-0.012), DINO-con=0.7373(-0.068). D9b: CLIP-S=0.7232(+0.007), 1-LPIPS=0.5766(-0.124), DINO-sty=0.4653(-0.011), DINO-con=0.7366(-0.069). D9c: CLIP-S=0.7224(+0.006), 1-LPIPS=0.5704(-0.131), DINO-sty=0.4623(-0.014), DINO-con=0.7301(-0.075). ROOT CAUSE: Increasing SWD weight increases CLIP-S (style affinity in CLIP space) but DECREASES DINO-sty. SWD matches marginal distributions (texture/color statistics), but DINO-sty measures semantic style similarity. More aggressive SWD = better texture matching but worse semantic style capture. The DINO-sty ceiling at 0.476 is NOT a loss balance limit — it is a fundamental limit of the SWD-based style injection mechanism. Loss reweighting is a DEAD END.
